newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares finish down, seen drifting.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares finish down, seen drifting.

text.p: Share prices ended broadly lower on Friday dragged down by institutional selling in leading stocks ahead of long weekend holidays at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), brokers said.
The 30-share BSE index finished 41.72 points, or 1.23 percent, lower at a provisional 3,349.82.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange (NSE) shed 8.19 points, 0.83 percent, at a provisional 980.01.
The 500-share CRISIL index dropped 7.32 points to a provisional 662.16.
Traders said foreign funds sold bank stocks SBI and Oriental Bank, steel firm TISCO, cement share ACC and Punjab Tractors.
The funds were buyers in Hind Lever, Thermax, ABB and MICO.
They said the market also attracted position-squaring on the last day of the weekly account on the BSE.
The BSE is closed on Monday and Tuesday for religious local holidays after the weekend.
But the NSE which operates from 24 centres across the country is open.
"There's no news to push the market," said dealer Ramnik Parikh. "Prices will remain depressed next week."
Broking firm James Capel B&K said in a report that the markets will remain depressed in the near-term as supply will exceed demand.
SBI fell 11.75 rupees to 261.25, TISCO 4.50 to 179, Reliance 4.0 to 199.25, ACC 51 to 1,973.25, ITC 3.25 to 287.75 and BSES 3.50 to 183.
TELCO dropped 7.25 rupees to 452.50, M&M 3.75 to 347.50 and Bajaj Auto 3.25 to 984.
EI Hotels rose 7.25 rupees to 637.25, Arvind Mills 2.50 to 123 and Hind Ciba 19.75 to 2,514.
